analysis:
This PR changes only documentation: docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (flowchart nodes at lines ~298-299, new reclaim text at lines ~338-372) and docs/architecture/inference.md (Nemotron Super eviction text at ~404-413, new paragraph on segment retention at ~1053-1073). No code, wire-protocol, key-handling, attestation or authorization surface changes. I found no documented change that weakens TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011 controls, and no change to the App Attest, receipt or authorization semantics.

The docs describe a provider-local memory behavior change that the next pass should check against code, which was not supplied. (1) Free 64 MiB paged KV segments from a released row are now parked per pool, up to min(2 GiB, grant/8). They sit outside the grant, floor and ledger charge. They are reinstalled for the next same-size admission and dropped on refusal, on a release request, or after 30 s idle. Security-relevant questions: whether reinstalled segments can expose a prior consumer's KV bytes (residual-data class T-028 and the A-001 prompt confidentiality asset) if they are not zeroed or if page-length bounds are not strictly enforced; and whether uncharged parked memory (up to 2 GiB per pool) could weaken the unified-cap and OOM guarantees (availability, T-010 and T-029 class). Parked data lengthens residual-KV lifetime in process memory by up to 30 s idle. This is in the same trust position as the existing T-011 and T-014 operator-memory exposure, but the threat model does not currently mention it, so T-028 may need a note. (2) New segments wrap zero-fill-on-demand host pages (cbv2ZeroFilledPages). This is a new but plausibly benign zeroing mechanism, and its correctness depends on code outside the supplied evidence. (3) The Nemotron Super load gate now releases retained segments before eviction and counts them as eviction credit only until the release. This is a memory-admission accuracy change with no apparent trust-boundary effect. (4) The idle cache sweep now runs inside WholeMacServiceBudget.performIfIdle. This adds a scheduling interaction but changes no data exposure.

The env kill switches DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP are local operator knobs. They do not affect the SSD prefix cache (T-041) or its encrypted at-rest posture, which the docs do not alter. No concrete regression is supported by the docs alone. The code claims (zeroing, uncharged parked bytes) are unverified here.
